title: check_dp_scope: two RFC 5280 §6.3.3(b) scope guards unpinned
description:
## Why

The `crl_applies_to` / `check_dp_scope` predicate answers RFC 5280 §6.3.3(b):
does this certificate's `cRLDistributionPoints` point at this CRL? Two of its
match guards survive mutation, and one of them is the fail-open direction.

## The survivors

    crl.rs:1893:33  replace match guard `crl_is_indirect` with true
    crl.rs:1897:21  replace match guard `names_match(crl_issuer, cert_issuer)` with true

1897 is the one that matters. The arm is

    None if names_match(crl_issuer, cert_issuer) => cert_issuer,
    None => continue,

so with the guard always true, a distribution point carrying no `cRLIssuer`
matches whatever CRL is presented, regardless of whether that CRL's issuer is
the certificate's issuer. A CRL from an unrelated CA then counts as in scope.

1893 is the converse direction: `Some(dn) if crl_is_indirect => dn` honours a
DP's named `cRLIssuer` only for a CRL that declares `indirectCRL`. Always
true, a direct CRL claims the scope of an indirect one.

## Open question to settle first

`check_revocation` already enforces `names_match(cert.issuer, crl.issuer)` for
direct CRLs via `enforce_direct_crl_domain`, which may make 1897 unreachable
from that entry point. The public `crl_applies_to` predicate shares the
implementation but not necessarily that gate -- read the two call paths before
building a fixture.

This is the same shape as the OCSP CertID key-hash half settled in
`ocsp_certid_binding.rs`: a guard that cannot be reached because an earlier
check subsumes it. If that is the answer here, record it in the test module
rather than contorting a fixture, and say which earlier check does the work.

## Found by

The first pkix-revocation mutation sweep, 2026-11-27: 276 mutants, 93 missed.
close_reason: Both guards pinned in 22114621. tests/dp_scope_guards.rs with fixtures/dp-scope/: the distribution-point names agree on both sides on purpose, so the issuer question is the only thing left to refuse on. The reachability question in the description resolved as reachable: crl_applies_to's own issuer gate covers direct CRLs only, so 1897 is live for an indirect CRL from an unrelated CA, and 1893 is live for a direct CRL against a DP that names a cRLIssuer. Each refusal asserts CrlDistributionPointIssuerMismatch specifically, because the weakened guards flip the reported half of the rule even where they do not flip the verdict.
